facts.text: Pathum Wan, literally 'lotus forest' from Pali paduma plus vana, was named after a royal villa erected there.
Next to the palace, a royal villa and the temple Wat Pathumwanaram were constructed, anchoring the district's early royal heritage.
During King Mongkut's reign, royal paddy fields between Khlong Phadung Krung Kasem and Ban Khrua were transformed into lotus‑laden ponds for leisure.
When the BTS Skytrain launched in 1999, Siam station became Pathum Wan's central interchange, solidifying its status as Bangkok's modern heart.
Hua Lamphong, Bangkok's main railway station built in 1916, occupies Pathum Wan's southwestern corner and once served as the city's main terminus.
The Jim Thompson House Museum in Pathum Wan preserves Thai silk history and was once the home of the American entrepreneur who revived the industry.
